description: Add a resilient New York wedding-date weather forecast widget and a persistent, accessible dark-mode experience while preserving the dependency-free static architecture and progressive enhancement.
steps: Add a discoverable weather section and navigation path in index.html for New York City on October 7 through October 9, 2026. Include useful no-JavaScript and pre-forecast copy, an accessible status region, forecast-card structure that JavaScript can populate without innerHTML, provider attribution, and a secure direct forecast link that remains useful when live data is unavailable.

Implement the runtime forecast flow in script.js using a no-key browser weather API suitable for latitude 40.7128, longitude -74.0060 and the America/New_York time zone. Request only the required daily fields and only when the event dates fall within the provider's supported forecast horizon. Render human-readable conditions, high and low temperatures, and precipitation chance for available event dates; handle malformed payloads, HTTP errors, offline/CORS failures, abort/timeout, dates outside the horizon, and past dates with clear fallback messaging. Preserve static itinerary content and avoid innerHTML.

Add an accessible dark-mode toggle in index.html and theme logic in script.js. Follow prefers-color-scheme when no explicit preference exists, persist an explicit light or dark choice in localStorage with storage access guarded against browser restrictions, keep aria-pressed and the visible/accessible label synchronized, respond to system preference changes only while no explicit choice is stored, update the theme-color metadata, and apply the selected theme early enough to avoid an obvious flash.

Extend styles.css using the existing custom-property and cascade-layer system so dark mode covers every light and dark surface, cards, borders, illustrations, text, controls, toast, weather states, and focus indicators at readable contrast. Style the weather widget responsively, keep controls at least 44px, support reduced motion and print, and ensure weather or theme controls do not crowd the 560px navigation layout.

Expand tests/site.test.js with meaningful coverage that executes or directly exercises the new forecast and theme paths using built-in Node.js and controlled browser/DOM/fetch/storage doubles. Cover available forecast rendering, outside-horizon and service-failure fallback behavior, persisted dark selection, default system preference, and safe storage failure. Retain focused HTML/CSS accessibility contracts for semantic status, secure external links, touch targets, dark palette contrast, reduced motion, and no third-party script/style assets.

Update scripts/validate.js so production validation includes the critical weather and theme contracts, update README.md with weather provider and forecast-horizon behavior, data/privacy and failure fallback, dark-mode behavior, project structure, and unchanged local commands, then run all verification and commit the complete implementation and task state locally with a descriptive commit without pushing.
acceptance_criteria: The page has a clearly discoverable weather widget for New York and the October 7 through October 9, 2026 event dates.

When the provider returns valid event-date data, the widget displays readable conditions, daily high and low temperatures, and precipitation probability; when data is too early, in the past, offline, malformed, or unavailable, it displays honest useful fallback copy and a direct forecast link without breaking the itinerary.

A keyboard-accessible, touch-friendly control switches between light and dark modes, announces its current action/state, persists an explicit choice across reloads, and otherwise follows the operating-system color preference.

Both themes remain responsive, readable, reduced-motion compatible, printable, and usable without JavaScript; external links are secured and no third-party script, stylesheet, font, image, or package dependency is introduced.
Meaningful automated tests fail if forecast rendering/fallback or theme selection/persistence logic is removed, and env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build plus env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test both pass.
The review-ready changes are committed locally on feat/weather-dark-mode and git status is clean, with no push or pull request creation.
verification: env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run dev, then inspect weather success/fallback and light/dark layouts at phone and desktop widths
findings: Added a semantic New York weather section for October 7-9, 2026 with static fallback cards, an accessible live status, Open-Meteo attribution, and a secure National Weather Service forecast link. Runtime logic requests only four required daily fields for fixed NYC coordinates and America/New_York when the complete date range is within Open-Meteo's 16-day horizon; it validates payloads and handles early, underway, past, offline/CORS, malformed, HTTP, and timeout paths without innerHTML. Added an early theme initializer plus an accessible 44px persisted toggle that follows system preference until an explicit choice, guards storage access, updates theme-color and aria state, and supports no-JavaScript system dark styling. Expanded responsive, reduced-motion, print, dark-surface, weather, and navigation CSS. Added controlled DOM/fetch/storage/media-query tests, bringing the suite to 17 passing tests, and expanded production validation and README documentation. env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build and env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test pass. Live headless inspection confirmed desktop and 390px layouts have no horizontal overflow, phone weather cards use one column, mobile navigation does not crowd, and the toggle is 44px high with synchronized dark state. No Dockerfile or remote exists, so no Docker build or push was performed. Semantic review remediation added an invariant light hero foreground, a dark-safe tip-label accent, and enhancement gating that keeps the theme toggle hidden until its click behavior is initialized. Regression coverage now checks hero and header gradient contrast, dark tip-label contrast, no-script toggle behavior, the inclusive forecast boundary, malformed payloads, HTTP errors, and request aborts. Production validation and all 19 tests pass. Desktop and 390px browser checks confirmed readable dark surfaces, a 44px toggle, one-column mobile weather cards, fallback weather copy, and no horizontal overflow. Semantic review remediation iteration 2 replaced the toggle's changing action name with the stable name Dark mode so aria-pressed unambiguously reports that option's state, and tests now assert the combined accessible announcement. Responsive rules were converted to mobile-first single-column defaults with min-width enhancements at 561px and 821px. Browser checks at 320px and 1280px confirmed no overflow, appropriate navigation density, 44px controls, and one or three weather columns as appropriate.
